options.label: A
options.description: Reject Corvane's bid as non-responsive based on failure to acknowledge Addendum 2 and omitted subcontractor designations; award to Tasker & Moye.

options.label: B
options.description: Re-bid the project to avoid litigation and ensure a clean award process.

options.label: C
options.description: Dismiss the protest immediately as untimely without evaluating the merits of the non-responsiveness claims.

options.label: A
options.note: This action is legally defensible because the failure to initial Addendum 2 is a facial defect that permits rejection, but it fails the client because it ignores the statutory requirement to verify the prime contractor's ability to self-perform or subcontract the fire sprinkler work, creating a high risk of a successful bid protest on the licensing ground.

options.label: B
options.note: Re-bidding is a lawful exercise of the agency's discretion to reject all bids, but it severely fails the client's objectives by pushing the switchgear release past the December 1 deadline and delaying the entire project schedule by months while exposing the district to higher market prices.

options.label: C
options.note: Dismissing the protest without evaluating the merits is unlawful because the licensing issue regarding the fire sprinkler system involves a substantive question of statutory compliance that cannot be resolved on timeliness alone, and it fails the client by potentially awarding a contract to an unqualified bidder.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have recommended holding the award decision until Corvane's written response is received on Tuesday, using a late supplement to the Board packet to present a conditional award or a recommendation for a responsibility hearing based on the new facts regarding the C-16 classification and the Copper Basin termination.
grade.overall: The consultation correctly identifies that the Addendum 2 defect is waivable but the licensing issue requires further fact-finding, yet it fails to recommend the only safe path: delaying the Board's vote until the bidder's response clarifies the C-16 status and the nature of the prior termination, thereby avoiding an unlawful rejection or an award to an unqualified contractor.
